newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET-ENGLAND AND NZ TIE ONE-DAY CLIFFHANGER.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ENGLAND AND NZ TIE ONE-DAY CLIFFHANGER.

text.p: A scrambled bye off the final ball enabled England to force a tie with New Zealand in a tense finish to the third one-day international on Wednesday.

After all-rounder Chris Harris had cut a swathe through the tourists' top batting, tailenders Darren Gough and Dominic Cork scampered a single to take England to 237 for eight. New Zealand had earlier been dismissed for 237 in two balls short of their 50 overs.

A half-century from Graham Thorpe, followed by useful knocks by Cork (31 not out) and Craig White (39), rescued England after Harris, with a spell of three for 20 from 10 overs, had threatened to swing the game decisively New Zealand's way.
He produced three near-identical inswinging yorkers to claim the prize wickets of Mike Atherton, Alec Stewart and Nasser Hussain, all clean bowled.
When Thorpe was caught behind off Simon Doull for 55, England were in trouble at 174 for six as Cork went to the wicket to join White.

Needing to score at more than a run a ball, they scurried between wickets, slogged and rode their luck -- especially when White survived a skier to square leg that miraculously fell between three fielders.
England needed eight to win from the last over, with left-armer Geoff Allott, in his first one-day international, bowling to Cork.
No run came from the first ball, and just a bye from the second as Cork swung and failed to make contact. White scored one from the third ball, but was run out going for the second.
Robert Croft raised England's hopes by hitting his first ball for four through the leg side. But needing two to win from two balls, he was bowled by the next delivery.
Gough failed to connect with the last ball of the innings which went straight through to wicketkeeper and captain Lee Germon, but the batsmen managed to scamper a bye.
The tie left England leading 2-0 in the five-match series. The fourth match is in Auckland on Saturday.
Opener Bryan Young had earlier provided the backbone of the New Zealand innings with a solid 53, but his fellow batsmen again failed to build on solid starts.
White was the best of the England bowlers with four for 37.
